title: Rectify phantom prefetch shadowing causing delayed refunds after rolling upgrades
creator: Ava Mitchell
description:
Summary: Multiple customers across Hosted, Dedicated and Private reported delayed refunds and negative invoice spikes after our Feb rolling upgrades. Investigation points to a race in the prefetch/KV-cache attribution path where stale prefetch entries from prior node generations were re-emitted with stale tenant attribution during failover/handback. This manifests as phantom 'prefetch' token lines that later get suppressed and trigger backward-facing credits once reconciled, producing invoice volatility.

Scope & Impact: Affected tenants: 7 confirmed enterprise tenants (mix of Hosted and Private). Observable effects: transient negative invoice lines, delayed refund jobs, skewed hourly usage curves, and accounting reconciliation alerts on downstream billing exports. Severity: customer-facing financial variance -> classified P0/high impact.

Root cause hypothesis: During rolling upgrades we introduced a lightweight prefetch cache migration that allowed pre-existing KV cache shards to be rehydrated by a background replication stream. The replication includes a short-lived attribution header that is overwritten by the new node only after a concurrent replay job re-emits prefetch events. If the node handback occurs while the old attribution stamp sits in the replication window, the prefetch emits with the old tenant alias and later gets deduplicated, causing a double-sided correction (initial phantom charge then refund). Timing window correlates with partial rolling upgrade timeline and high traffic windows.

Steps to reproduce (dev/staging):
1. Stand up two-node private cluster with staged rolling upgrade.
2. Seed KV prefetch entries under tenant T-A; start heavy short-lived prefetch traffic.
3. Trigger handback from node-v1 -> node-v2 while kicking an async replication rehydrate job.
4. Observe prefetch emission logs include previous attribution header; compare metering ledger and final invoice export.

Immediate mitigation (already deployed):
- Hotfix v1.22.1: we added an attribution verification gate in the prefetch emission pipeline to drop events with non-current node stamps. Deployed to Hosted canaries 2026-03-02 and to affected Private clusters on customer request by 2026-03-05.
- Emergency billing backfill: finance ran a manual adjustment script (billing-adjust-v2) to suppress phantom lines for 7 tenants; refunds queued.

Planned fix (this ticket):
- Implement authoritative attribution handshake for prefetch replay path (server-side): ensure rehydrated KV entries must be re-validated before any emit; add idempotency token (prefetch-emission-id) persisted with ledger write.
- Add unit and integration tests to simulate rolling upgrade handback and prefetch rehydrate races.
- Add metric and alert: prefetch-attribution-mismatch.count and prefetch-emit-dropped.count.
- Coordinate with Billing team to add conservative suppression window in invoice exporter for 48 hours post-upgrade.

Acceptance criteria:
- Integration tests covering the race pass in CI with deterministic timeouts.
- No phantom prefetch lines observed in canary hosted during a controlled rolling upgrade test.
- Metrics: prefetch-attribution-mismatch.count <= 0 and prefetch-emit-dropped.count > 0 for upgrades; ledger reconciliation downstream shows no negative invoice spikes in 72 hours after canary.

Rollout plan:
1. Merge PR and run full CI (runtime/integration/billing-export tests) — owner: Diego Ramos.
2. Canary deploy runtime-1.22.2 to two hosted clusters during low-traffic window (03:00 UTC) — monitor metrics and ledgers for 6 hours.
3. If stable, coordinate with SRE to schedule Dedicated and Private channel upgrade wave (customer opt-in) over next 48 hours.
4. Post-deploy: run reconciliation job for last 7 days in dry-run mode, then apply adjustments where needed.

Monitoring & dashboards:
- Dashboard links: billing-reconciliation: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/billing/reconciliation, prefetch-emits: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/prefetch/emit-health
- Runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Prefetch+Attribution+Runbook (initial edits added).

Customer comms:
- CS owners: Priya Nair (Hosted), Markus Vogel (Enterprise success). Draft customer message prepared: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1-prefetch-customer-note (internal link).
- Refunds: finance ticket FIN-412 created; estimated refund amount $82,450 across affected tenants.

Notes & decisions:
- Trade-off: adding handshake increases prefetch latency by ~0.8ms on average in microbenchmarks. We accept this for stability given financial impact; plan to optimize later with batched handshake.
- Security review: not required for this change (no secrets), but change added a persisted idempotency token; will note for audit logs.

Follow-ups (post-closure):
- Retro: schedule 1-hour postmortem with SRE/Billing/Support/CX.
- Explore prefetch TTL tuning to reduce replication window.
- Add a synthetic test to nightly that runs a rolling upgrade scenario against staging.
